cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO
geo.gloss: Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers.

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: OpenAI adds product carousels and AppsFlyer attribution to compete for ad dollars
stories.plain: ChatGPT is adding shoppable product carousels and performance attribution via AppsFlyer, moving it from an experimental ad channel to a measurable one. This matters because it signals OpenAI wants a slice of performance marketing budgets, forcing marketers to rethink where they allocate spend and how GEO fits their channel mix.

stories.head: How to manage AI prompt governance and costs at scale
stories.plain: A practical guide to building centralized prompt libraries and token-budget controls so AI content generation stays on-brand and on-budget. As teams scale GenAI output, ungoverned prompts create brand risk and runaway API costs — this framework shows how to set the guardrails before they become urgent problems.

stories.head: Viral Nation launches AI Discovery, a social-first GEO service to shape brand signals in AI answers
stories.plain: Viral Nation's new Generative Engine Optimization offering helps brands influence how AI systems like ChatGPT and Perplexity surface and describe them, using social signals and authority-building rather than traditional SEO. This is an early commercial product in the fast-emerging GEO category, relevant to any marketer worried about visibility in AI-generated answers.

stories.head: 5 AI blind spots that cost conversions — what generates copy vs. what changes behavior
stories.plain: The piece argues that most marketers misuse AI by optimizing for output volume rather than behavioral impact, identifying five specific gaps between generating competent copy and actually moving customers to act. Useful for teams measuring GenAI ROI and wondering why conversion rates haven't budged despite faster content production.

stories.head: Echovane raises $1M to deliver end-to-end AI-agent market research for Fortune 500 brands
stories.plain: Echovane, backed by alumni from Amazon and Stripe, uses AI agents to run full market research studies autonomously — design, fieldwork, and synthesis — for clients like P&G and Kantar. It signals that agentic AI is moving into research budgets, potentially disrupting traditional insights vendors and changing how marketers gather audience intelligence.

stories.head: OpenAI adds product carousels and AppsFlyer attribution to compete for ad dollars
stories.plain: ChatGPT now shows shoppable product carousels and connects to AppsFlyer for performance attribution — two features that let marketers measure ROI inside an AI answer engine. This moves OpenAI from an experimental ad channel to a serious competitor for performance budgets, and forces brands to think about GEO alongside paid search.

stories.head: How to manage AI prompt governance and costs at scale
stories.plain: As teams scale AI content generation, runaway token costs and off-brand outputs are real risks. This guide lays out centralized prompt governance frameworks — version control, spending caps, and brand guardrails — that keep AI content production safe and affordable. Directly relevant to anyone buying or building martech stacks with generative AI.

stories.head: Time magazine serves ads directly to AI crawlers in a novel GEO strategy
stories.plain: Time is experimenting with ads targeted at AI crawlers rather than human readers — a tactic designed to plant brand signals inside the training and retrieval pipelines that power AI-generated answers. If it works, it creates an entirely new media-buying category that bypasses traditional display and search entirely.

stories.head: Viral Nation launches AI Discovery, a social-first Generative Engine Optimization service
stories.plain: Viral Nation is selling a managed service that shapes the social signals and authority cues AI systems use when deciding which brands to surface in answers. This is one of the first agency offerings to package GEO as a productized retainer, signaling that generative engine visibility is moving from experiment to budget line item.

stories.head: Klaviyo acquires AI startup Agency, names founder Elias Torres chief product officer
stories.plain: Klaviyo bought the AI startup Agency and brought its founder in as CPO — a move that signals the CEP market is consolidating around agentic capabilities. For marketers evaluating email and SMS platforms, this acquisition suggests Klaviyo is building toward autonomous campaign execution rather than just assisted drafting.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: OpenAI & AI-Native Ad Platforms Enter the Arena
body: OpenAI's move to build advertising technology signals that the companies controlling large language models now want a direct cut of the $600B+ global ad market. This is not a product update — it redraws the competitive map, putting AI labs in direct competition with Google, Meta, and the programmatic stack.

Simultaneously, Viral Nation's GEO offering and Time's AI-only ad formats show that generative-engine optimization is becoming a real budget line. Brands that still plan only for search and social are already missing the channel where the next generation of consumer discovery is being built.

themes.head: The Human-Judgment Premium Rises
body: At AI4 2026 — which drew 12,000 leaders from 100 countries, a 50% attendance jump — the loudest practitioner voice was not about automation speed but about when to override the model. Big Spaceship's CEO Taryn Crouthers framed human judgment as a deliberate organizational capability, not a fallback.

MarTech's own reporting on AI blind spots and the skills AI makes more valuable echoes the same shift: strategic empathy, contextual reasoning, and cross-functional translation are appreciating assets precisely because they are hard to automate. The decision for teams is no longer 'adopt AI' but 'which judgments do we keep human, and why.'

themes.head: Prompt Governance & Cost Control Become Infrastructure
body: As AI usage scales inside marketing orgs, runaway inference costs and inconsistent outputs are surfacing as real operational risks. MarTech's governance guide marks a turning point: AI prompts are now assets that need version control, ownership, and audit trails — just like code or brand guidelines.

This theme connects directly to platform-level observability investment (groundcover's Gartner recognition) and to the broader pattern of enterprises realizing that ungoverned AI spend compounds quietly until it shows up as a budget crisis or a compliance problem. Governance frameworks built now will be competitive moats in 18 months.

themes.head: Identity & Addressability Get an AI Upgrade
body: MobileFuse's partnership with Adstra and PubMatic's new CRO hire — explicitly tied to AI transforming digital advertising — reflect a convergent bet: identity resolution and audience addressability are the foundational layer that makes AI-driven targeting valuable rather than speculative. Without clean identity data, generative ad tools optimise noise.

For decision-makers this means the identity stack is no longer a back-end plumbing question — it is the primary determinant of whether AI personalization investments deliver ROI. First-party data quality and interoperability with independent identity graphs are now C-suite concerns, not just data-engineering ones.

themes.head: Agencies & Org Design Must Catch Up with AI
body: Two distinct but reinforcing pieces — MarTech on agency evolution and Criteo's Todd Parsons on org charts misaligned with customer journeys — land the same verdict: current organizational structures were designed for a pre-AI world and actively slow down AI adoption. The bottleneck is not technology; it is reporting lines and incentive design.

The framing from 'The future belongs to marketers who make others smarter' adds a talent corollary: the most valuable marketing role is now the AI-enabled multiplier who raises the capability of every adjacent team. Agencies and in-house teams that reorganize around this model will out-execute those still structured around channel ownership.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack this month, the real stakes are not which AI tools to adopt but who controls the identity data, governance infrastructure, and human judgment calls that make AI outputs trustworthy and commercially defensible.
